questions.learningObjective: Distinguish avoir verbs from etre verbs
questions.stem: Which sentence uses the wrong auxiliary?
questions.explanation: Ils ont alle uses avoir with a movement verb, which is wrong. Aller takes etre.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Explain etre agreement with a feminine subject
questions.stem: Explain how the participle agrees when a feminine subject uses etre.

answer.exemplar: With etre, the participle takes the feminine form to match a feminine subject, adding an e to the masculine form.

questions.explanation: Etre verbs agree with the subject, so a feminine subject requires the feminine participle form.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Decide agreement with a following direct object

stimulus.body: The dispatcher checked the signals after the shift.

questions.stem: In the passage, does the participle agree with signals?

options.text: Yes, because the subject is feminine
Yes, because signals is the object
No, because signals follows the verb

questions.explanation: Signals follows the verb, so it does not trigger agreement. Only a preceding direct object does.
questions.hint: Following object does not trigger agreement.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.learningObjective: Negate a sentence in a dispatcher log
questions.stem: Stage one: a log sentence is negative. Stage two: place ne and pas correctly.

options.text: Ne before, pas after the conjugated verb

questions.explanation: Ne precedes and pas follows the conjugated verb. Other placements break the negation rule.
questions.hint: Ne before, pas after the verb.
